content.content:
# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- The scouting logins are global demo logins shared by every team: local bid-form and TAN runs collide with other
  teams (TAN request numbers jump). Verify TAN signing with test runs, which get fresh logins (up to 5 per team at
  once, 3 more waiting); see the isolation probe below for what else is shared.
- Isolation probe (two browser contexts, scouting login): the bid wizard's progress lives in the session cookie, not
  the account (A advanced to step 2, a fresh context B still saw an empty step 1), so local bid-form runs do not see
  each other's wizard. The webmail is one shared mailbox (same list in both contexts, TAN mails numbered across all
  teams), so TAN requests remain the only collision: stop local runs before the TAN request, sign in test runs.
- Scouting logins are shared by all teams: TAN request numbers are global and a request from another team
  invalidates ours (local runs saw "Anforderung 59" rejected after someone requested 60). The bid wizard state is
  per browser session, so local runs are fine for the form phase; measure signing only in test runs
  (`AGENT_STOP_BEFORE_SIGN=1` stops a local run before the TAN request).
- Bid speed-up, test runs: baseline 201 s; two phases (form thinking off, review thinking on) 271 s (one run:
  documents detour, mail lookup hit its step limit, slow thinking steps); review thinking off too 171 s;
  final variant 94, 96, 105 and 87 s (4 runs), quality 10 each, cost $0.008 to $0.010 instead of $0.019.
- Final variant: form phase thinking off with fill_in() (several form actions per step), then one thinking-off
  model call checks the review page, then the signing phase (thinking off unless the check fails or finds
  problems) uses request_signing_tan(ref), which clicks the model-chosen button and fetches the TAN in one tool.
- Summary check offline test (6 doctored review pages: ok, alternative offer, 5 % discount, position not
  omitted, extra position, transposed VAT id): thinking off 6/6 in 2 to 5 s, thinking on 6/6 in 4 to 27 s.
- Briefing with thinking off is correct (validated against the brief) and takes 6 to 10 s instead of 17 to 45 s.
- Thinking-off form steps sometimes click the wrong ref on the one-position-per-step configurator ("add
  position" instead of "next"); the summary check and the goal's "never use options that add positions" catch it.
- Goal wording costs time: "acknowledge the tender documents" sent the model to read every document (35 s);
  "tick the form's acknowledgement (no need to open them)" fixed it.
- After the bid is in, the platform closes the run's model token; the final model call gets 401. Caught now.
- Faster v1 submission (thinking by phase, fill_in, TAN hand-off): quality 10 in 2:34 min for $0.011, against 4:41 and
  $0.024 for the first v1; no quality loss, cost x time about 4x better.
- Page views, read-only bench (smoke goals, 3 runs each, base vs new): the history trim kept only the newest request's
  view, so after any note() the model had no page at all and invented values (refused notes, re-opened pages). Now
  the latest view stays until a newer one arrives, and the first prompt's view is trimmed once superseded.
- Same-page actions now return only the changed parts (controls are separate pieces, unchanged refs stay valid) or
  "unchanged"; the full view stays in context and in the cached prefix. Invented form (fill, select, tick, save):
  ~27.7k -> ~20.6k input tokens, correct in 7/7 runs. Read-only sites navigate, so diffs rarely fire there.
- Select lists over 600 characters show count, first 8 and last 2; `options(ref, contains)` searches them and a
  failed `select` names close matches. Costs one request when the model wants the list, saves tokens per view.
- Request makeup (smoke): system + tools ~5k chars fixed, history ~3k, view ~1.5-2.5k; 40-55 % of input is reported
  as cached, so per-request token cuts are modest; the step count dominates tokens and seconds (browser actions
  take 0.3-0.7 s, a model step 1-4 s). Repeated boilerplate lines (footer, title bar) were 1-4 % of view text when
  restricted to safe lines: not worth the risk of hiding status lines, dropped.
- Clef vs Qwen offline eval (`dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md`, 68 hand-labelled decisions from real page views, 3
  repeats): Clef answers in ~1 s and is deterministic, but loses to Qwen at picking links (79 % vs 93 % thinking
  off) and at judging the right record (88 % vs 98 % thinking on; it takes `<ref>-A` look-alikes for the exact
  reference and misses ordering such as "highest request number"). It is exact at "is this an error, empty, locked
  or decoy page after my action" (100 % vs 93 % for Qwen off, same speed). Kept only that check, behind
  `AGENT_CLEF=1` (`page_check` tool); Clef's `score` criteria must be a list, and many `noul` questions fit one call.
- Site tools (`site_tools.py` search / collect / extract), local read-only check against the scouting sites: an ERP
  search that the site refuses as too broad took 10 steps, 46 s and 34k input tokens with the tools (remark reported
  right) against 30 steps, 153 s, 112k and no answer without; a mailbox search over inbox and archive took 18 steps
  and 105 s with the tools (10 messages over 3 pages each, newest right), plain stopped at 30 steps or hung on
  re-locking gates. Two fixes were needed: older tool results were cut to one line once a newer view came, so the
  model paged again by hand to see the list it had collected (results of search / collect / extract now stay), and
  after paging the next view must come whole, not as a diff against a page the model never saw.
- v2 position filling (`configurator.py`, `PositionDesk` in `submit.py`): the model names the position on screen,
  maps control labels to value names once and names the confirm button; the helper walks the cascading selects
  one level per round trip, matches options by value (text-sorted lists, neighbouring numbers or a catalogue
  number that is a prefix of another) and formats German numbers. Offline mock and live (scouting, up to the TAN
  page): one position entered in full, a position with an impossible attribute failed and was omitted, net total
  from the entered positions only, Hauptangebot, AGB unticked; 202 s, 28 requests, 183k input tokens.
- The worker forgot the page after a note(): `_forget_old_views` kept only the last request, so a short tool
  result wiped the newest view and Qwen clicked guessed refs (hit "add position" in the mock). Keep the newest view
  in full whatever comes after it.
- Attribute wording can differ from the option text (a "none" attribute vs a "without ..." option): the tool
  reports the options and the model passes `choices`, used only when no option matches literally (an always-on
  override broke a later position that was already right).
- Without "every value is already calculated; do not research" the bid worker wandered into documents and the Q&A
  and burned its 76 steps picking options itself. The goal now says so up front.
- Phased flow (form phase thinking off) on the offline mock: positions, discount, net total, offer type and
  declarations right, summary check matched, signed in 93 s and 16 requests. Thinking-off slips seen there and
  live: the model typed its own net total (now stated in the goal), clicked "omit" on a position without asking
  configure_position() (goal: call it first on every position page), sent a partial `fields` map that replaced
  the first one and let an unrelated position count as entered (maps now merge; a position counts only with
  material, quantity, price and lead time mapped), and "chose" a neighbouring bore for an impossible one via
  `choices` (numbers must now match exactly; `choices` only for worded attributes, remembered per position).
- Live on the shared scouting login, a re-login mid-run reset the wizard to its first step; the worker re-entered
  the form from the start. Another reason to verify signing only in test runs.
- Live, thinking off, the model still entered its own "all positions" net total after one position failed and
  clicked "omit" instead of "next" right after a successful fill (that position was lost). Now every
  configure_position() result states the running net total of the positions entered, and the tool saves the
  position with the next button the model named once. Mock after that: signed and fully correct in 64 s,
  13 requests.
- Local live runs twice hung before the briefing finished: one site's start (the webmail) never returned while the
  sites answered curl at once. solve() gathers every site start without a timeout; worth a guard.
- Streaming through the models proxy (raw SSE probes): text and `reasoning_content` arrive token by token (gaps
  under 1.5 s), but tool-call arguments are held back until complete (a 60-row output tool: first argument byte at
  64 s, all at once); quiet stretches carry `: keepalive` comments every 10 s. Headers come with the first (role)
  chunk: within 9.4 s in 179 of 180 calls (p90 5.9 s, either mode). The one hang (thinking off) sent no headers
  and nothing else for 200 s, so "no first chunk in 20 s" catches it; a tool call's silence cannot be told from a
  stall, so tool requests keep their per-mode timeout as allowed silence.
- `LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1` A/B (30 agent calls each, run side by side): excluding one prompt that sends thinking-on
  reasoning into minutes, median 13.2 s vs 14.4 s, p90 74 vs 81 s, max 89 vs 268 s (deadline retried a legit
  thinking-on long answer twice); 2 no-first-chunk retries caught at 20 s. On the runaway-reasoning prompt the
  deadline failed 2 of 8 after 6 retries x 90 s, the watchdog finished 8 of 8 but took 87 to 811 s (6 calls hit
  the 300 s cap). Progress does not end runaway reasoning: keep the cap lower (LLM_MAX_CALL 120 to 150) or cap
  output tokens before turning the watchdog on.
- v2 orchestrator local runs (planner -> board -> workers -> verify -> calc): the planner picked all four fact kinds
  and mapped each to the right site from the brief alone (23 s); the tender worker resolved 5 positions with final
  quantities and keys in 75 to 105 s; the mail plan named 9 record kinds. `Trace.event()` takes `kind` and `worker`
  positionally, so board events must not pass keywords of those names (two runs lost every posted fact to that).
- The spec worker (`research.py`, thinking off) twice looped between two controls on one page for its full 25
  steps and found no revision history, so no requirement reached the ERP; it needs a loop guard or thinking on
  for that step. Mail kinds that find nothing burn the full 20-step budget (about 70 s per kind and tab).
- A thinking verifier call over a batch of facts can outlast a 120 s budget; verify runs thinking off with the
  long-timeout reader model by default.
- v2 end to end, local (planner -> board -> tender, spec + ERP, mail -> verify -> calc): one run reached the full
  answer (local check 100/100) in 752 s of research; other runs lost the spec (navigator paged between two list
  pages for 25 steps, or clicked row menus the popup closer shut), the mail tabs (sign-ins hung or landed on the
  browser error page) or the ERP (a look() wrapper missing the new keywords). Each now has a guard: a loop hint
  after three arrivals on one page, one thinking retry for the spec, time-limited starts with a retry that also
  rejects error pages, staggered mail tabs that join when ready, and a mail deadline with partial results.
- Mail records only count with the bidder's domain: when the address lookup ran on a tab that showed an error
  page, every authority record was dropped silently. The address now comes from the first tab that shows it.
- A requirement whose stroke reserve was not found came back without a material and calc turned the whole bid
  into no_bid. Undecided materials (pending inputs, search problems) now omit the position; only a complete
  search without a match means no_bid.
- One run with the mail kinds on site_tools.search/collect kept nothing in three kinds (150 s each; paging
  followed a message list into a session expiry); kept on the paging tool for now.
- First v2 sandbox test run (orchestrator branch 405b1f4): quality 100, eligible, about 10 min, 308 model calls,
  $0.134. The full pipeline works in the sandbox; the variance across repeats decides what to submit.
- v2 round 1 (4 sandbox test runs of 405b1f4): 100 (10 min), 100 with the watchdog (15 min), 10 (spec navigator
  found no revision history, so every position was omitted and the found discount was lost too), and NO BID: a false
  summary-check alarm switched signing to thinking, the model went back in the wizard (clears later steps) and the
  deadline cut it before the TAN was entered. Signing needs its own time reserve and must never go back.
- sub_9bd976b00673121a (quality 100, 14:02, rank #2) was the watchdog test run promoted to a submission from its run
  page. Its exact code is branch submitted/sub_9bd976b0. It still has the old signing weakness (no bid when signing
  overruns), so replace it once the fixed version scores 100 reliably across several test runs.
- Soak run 1 (3f5d6b6): NO BID. The sites were slow (several tabs hit the 45 s settle cap at once), the webmail
  session failed both starts and lost its tab, and submit_bid's address lookup then crashed on the empty tab list
  (IndexError), which ended solve() before signing. Fixed: sessions reopen a lost tab, mail lookups never raise,
  solve() retries signing once after an unexpected error.
- Spec redundancy (branch spec-redundancy): a fast and a thinking spec navigator run at once in separate contexts,
  the first with a revision and requirements wins; a stopped navigator still gets its revisions read from its last
  page. Tender documents and Q&A run in two tabs and positions post before the Q&A; a run without complete positions
  still answers (reference, decision, discount, total 0). Test runs: 100 (12.5 min, $0.177) and 100 (13.5 min, $0.184); one earlier run had a
  full research answer (82 offline) but signing timed out (fixed on main by the signing reserve).
- Mail research, local (scouting, 4 tabs): before 7 of 9 kinds in 515 s (plan 97 s after a 45 s stalled call;
  stalled reader calls held kinds 180 s; approval 330 s). After pipelined reads, a 60 s grace after the first
  hit, shorter read/plan timeouts and a fresh tab after 45 s without a page view: 8 of 9 in 401 s (plan 20 s,
  approval 106 s). Session expiry while opening a message's reading pane gave the reader a sign-in page (empty
  record); messages are now reopened when the tab landed elsewhere. Without the mailbox address, records are
  authorised by the recipients' domain instead of all being dropped.
- sub_63a81b12d47a68b9 (promoted from soak run run_262c91398cd64598): quality 100 in 7:33 for $0.110, rank #2.
  Final candidate since 22:17 UTC; exact code is 8c7ab8f (branch submitted/sub_63a81b12). Same code over 6 soak

  enters the bid position the page shows and lists the ones still to enter; early returns are traced.

  for an attribute the form has no control for failed whole positions; one live run mapped no price breakdown

  the first position page's controls (~30-50 s, during research), then waits. Sandbox run 07b5 (quality 100):

# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- The scouting logins are global demo logins shared by every team: local bid-form and TAN runs collide with other
  teams (TAN request numbers jump). Verify TAN signing with test runs, which get fresh logins (up to 5 per team at
  once, 3 more waiting); see the isolation probe below for what else is shared.
- Isolation probe (two browser contexts, scouting login): the bid wizard's progress lives in the session cookie, not
  the account (A advanced to step 2, a fresh context B still saw an empty step 1), so local bid-form runs do not see
  each other's wizard. The webmail is one shared mailbox (same list in both contexts, TAN mails numbered across all
  teams), so TAN requests remain the only collision: stop local runs before the TAN request, sign in test runs.
- Scouting logins are shared by all teams: TAN request numbers are global and a request from another team
  invalidates ours (local runs saw "Anforderung 59" rejected after someone requested 60). The bid wizard state is
  per browser session, so local runs are fine for the form phase; measure signing only in test runs
  (`AGENT_STOP_BEFORE_SIGN=1` stops a local run before the TAN request).
- Bid speed-up, test runs: baseline 201 s; two phases (form thinking off, review thinking on) 271 s (one run:
  documents detour, mail lookup hit its step limit, slow thinking steps); review thinking off too 171 s;
  final variant 94, 96, 105 and 87 s (4 runs), quality 10 each, cost $0.008 to $0.010 instead of $0.019.
- Final variant: form phase thinking off with fill_in() (several form actions per step), then one thinking-off
  model call checks the review page, then the signing phase (thinking off unless the check fails or finds
  problems) uses request_signing_tan(ref), which clicks the model-chosen button and fetches the TAN in one tool.
- Summary check offline test (6 doctored review pages: ok, alternative offer, 5 % discount, position not
  omitted, extra position, transposed VAT id): thinking off 6/6 in 2 to 5 s, thinking on 6/6 in 4 to 27 s.
- Briefing with thinking off is correct (validated against the brief) and takes 6 to 10 s instead of 17 to 45 s.
- Thinking-off form steps sometimes click the wrong ref on the one-position-per-step configurator ("add
  position" instead of "next"); the summary check and the goal's "never use options that add positions" catch it.
- Goal wording costs time: "acknowledge the tender documents" sent the model to read every document (35 s);
  "tick the form's acknowledgement (no need to open them)" fixed it.
- After the bid is in, the platform closes the run's model token; the final model call gets 401. Caught now.
- Faster v1 submission (thinking by phase, fill_in, TAN hand-off): quality 10 in 2:34 min for $0.011, against 4:41 and
  $0.024 for the first v1; no quality loss, cost x time about 4x better.
- Page views, read-only bench (smoke goals, 3 runs each, base vs new): the history trim kept only the newest request's
  view, so after any note() the model had no page at all and invented values (refused notes, re-opened pages). Now
  the latest view stays until a newer one arrives, and the first prompt's view is trimmed once superseded.
- Same-page actions now return only the changed parts (controls are separate pieces, unchanged refs stay valid) or
  "unchanged"; the full view stays in context and in the cached prefix. Invented form (fill, select, tick, save):
  ~27.7k -> ~20.6k input tokens, correct in 7/7 runs. Read-only sites navigate, so diffs rarely fire there.
- Select lists over 600 characters show count, first 8 and last 2; `options(ref, contains)` searches them and a
  failed `select` names close matches. Costs one request when the model wants the list, saves tokens per view.
- Request makeup (smoke): system + tools ~5k chars fixed, history ~3k, view ~1.5-2.5k; 40-55 % of input is reported
  as cached, so per-request token cuts are modest; the step count dominates tokens and seconds (browser actions
  take 0.3-0.7 s, a model step 1-4 s). Repeated boilerplate lines (footer, title bar) were 1-4 % of view text when
  restricted to safe lines: not worth the risk of hiding status lines, dropped.
- Clef vs Qwen offline eval (`dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md`, 68 hand-labelled decisions from real page views, 3
  repeats): Clef answers in ~1 s and is deterministic, but loses to Qwen at picking links (79 % vs 93 % thinking
  off) and at judging the right record (88 % vs 98 % thinking on; it takes `<ref>-A` look-alikes for the exact
  reference and misses ordering such as "highest request number"). It is exact at "is this an error, empty, locked
  or decoy page after my action" (100 % vs 93 % for Qwen off, same speed). Kept only that check, behind
  `AGENT_CLEF=1` (`page_check` tool); Clef's `score` criteria must be a list, and many `noul` questions fit one call.
- Site tools (`site_tools.py` search / collect / extract), local read-only check against the scouting sites: an ERP
  search that the site refuses as too broad took 10 steps, 46 s and 34k input tokens with the tools (remark reported
  right) against 30 steps, 153 s, 112k and no answer without; a mailbox search over inbox and archive took 18 steps
  and 105 s with the tools (10 messages over 3 pages each, newest right), plain stopped at 30 steps or hung on
  re-locking gates. Two fixes were needed: older tool results were cut to one line once a newer view came, so the
  model paged again by hand to see the list it had collected (results of search / collect / extract now stay), and
  after paging the next view must come whole, not as a diff against a page the model never saw.
- v2 position filling (`configurator.py`, `PositionDesk` in `submit.py`): the model names the position on screen,
  maps control labels to value names once and names the confirm button; the helper walks the cascading selects
  one level per round trip, matches options by value (text-sorted lists, neighbouring numbers or a catalogue
  number that is a prefix of another) and formats German numbers. Offline mock and live (scouting, up to the TAN
  page): one position entered in full, a position with an impossible attribute failed and was omitted, net total
  from the entered positions only, Hauptangebot, AGB unticked; 202 s, 28 requests, 183k input tokens.
- The worker forgot the page after a note(): `_forget_old_views` kept only the last request, so a short tool
  result wiped the newest view and Qwen clicked guessed refs (hit "add position" in the mock). Keep the newest view
  in full whatever comes after it.
- Attribute wording can differ from the option text (a "none" attribute vs a "without ..." option): the tool
  reports the options and the model passes `choices`, used only when no option matches literally (an always-on
  override broke a later position that was already right).
- Without "every value is already calculated; do not research" the bid worker wandered into documents and the Q&A
  and burned its 76 steps picking options itself. The goal now says so up front.
- Phased flow (form phase thinking off) on the offline mock: positions, discount, net total, offer type and
  declarations right, summary check matched, signed in 93 s and 16 requests. Thinking-off slips seen there and
  live: the model typed its own net total (now stated in the goal), clicked "omit" on a position without asking
  configure_position() (goal: call it first on every position page), sent a partial `fields` map that replaced
  the first one and let an unrelated position count as entered (maps now merge; a position counts only with
  material, quantity, price and lead time mapped), and "chose" a neighbouring bore for an impossible one via
  `choices` (numbers must now match exactly; `choices` only for worded attributes, remembered per position).
- Live on the shared scouting login, a re-login mid-run reset the wizard to its first step; the worker re-entered
  the form from the start. Another reason to verify signing only in test runs.
- Live, thinking off, the model still entered its own "all positions" net total after one position failed and
  clicked "omit" instead of "next" right after a successful fill (that position was lost). Now every
  configure_position() result states the running net total of the positions entered, and the tool saves the
  position with the next button the model named once. Mock after that: signed and fully correct in 64 s,
  13 requests.
- Local live runs twice hung before the briefing finished: one site's start (the webmail) never returned while the
  sites answered curl at once. solve() gathers every site start without a timeout; worth a guard.
- Streaming through the models proxy (raw SSE probes): text and `reasoning_content` arrive token by token (gaps
  under 1.5 s), but tool-call arguments are held back until complete (a 60-row output tool: first argument byte at
  64 s, all at once); quiet stretches carry `: keepalive` comments every 10 s. Headers come with the first (role)
  chunk: within 9.4 s in 179 of 180 calls (p90 5.9 s, either mode). The one hang (thinking off) sent no headers
  and nothing else for 200 s, so "no first chunk in 20 s" catches it; a tool call's silence cannot be told from a
  stall, so tool requests keep their per-mode timeout as allowed silence.
- `LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1` A/B (30 agent calls each, run side by side): excluding one prompt that sends thinking-on
  reasoning into minutes, median 13.2 s vs 14.4 s, p90 74 vs 81 s, max 89 vs 268 s (deadline retried a legit
  thinking-on long answer twice); 2 no-first-chunk retries caught at 20 s. On the runaway-reasoning prompt the
  deadline failed 2 of 8 after 6 retries x 90 s, the watchdog finished 8 of 8 but took 87 to 811 s (6 calls hit
  the 300 s cap). Progress does not end runaway reasoning: keep the cap lower (LLM_MAX_CALL 120 to 150) or cap
  output tokens before turning the watchdog on.
- v2 orchestrator local runs (planner -> board -> workers -> verify -> calc): the planner picked all four fact kinds
  and mapped each to the right site from the brief alone (23 s); the tender worker resolved 5 positions with final
  quantities and keys in 75 to 105 s; the mail plan named 9 record kinds. `Trace.event()` takes `kind` and `worker`

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
  organizers' reason.
- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.

Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
get the team disqualified.

## Flagged results

A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
lists flagged results, without a rank.
=== faq
# FAQ and event details

## FAQ

**Which models can I use?** The hosted models are free, and the starter kit shows how to call them. Or bring your own key for
any provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, or others the
organizers add) and send its calls through the metering proxy. `GET /v1/runs/current` lists the proxy base URLs. Models must have a published
price (a model too new for the platform's list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it; OpenRouter reports its own)
and satisfy any organizer model allowlist. See
[the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) for SDK setup.

**Where do I keep my model key?** As a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets): the team page's Secrets list
injects it into your agent's run step in test and scored runs, redacted from logs. Don't put keys in your
package; we store packages and the review agent reads them.

**Why does my model call get a 401?** "Add your OpenAI API key to the request" means no provider key arrived: set
`OPENAI_API_KEY` (in test and scored runs, as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets)). A 401 from the
provider itself means the key is wrong. Check that `OPENAI_BASE_URL` points at the run's proxy
(`$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1`, already set in test and scored runs); the same holds for any OpenAI-compatible provider.

**How do my teammates and I sign in from a terminal?** Each person runs `atira login` on their own computer
and approves it in the browser. Every device gets its own token; there is no shared team key to pass around.
Without a browser on the machine, `atira login --device` prints a link and a code to approve elsewhere.

**I lost a laptop, or a token leaked.** Revoke that device's token on your team page under Signed-in devices
(`atira logout` revokes the one on the computer you are at). Leaving or being removed from a team ends your
tokens' access to it at once.

**My invite link says it is for someone else.** Invites are for one GitHub account. Sign in with the account
the captain invited, or ask the captain to invite your GitHub username.

**Does it cost me anything?** We charge nothing, and the models the platform hosts are free and never charged. If
you bring your own key for another provider, that provider bills your key. The proxy measures every call and
ranks you on its cost at the published prices; hosted calls count at simulated API prices.

**How can I try my agent?** Develop locally against the public websites (`atira scout --env` exports the
scouting logins), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run ./my-agent`). A test run runs on `public-1`, the public
RFQ scenario, and returns your score with the points for each part of the answer. With the scouting logins nothing
counts: a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.

**Is the public scenario's answer published?** No. The correct answer isn't published; your system has to work it
out from the websites. Score breakdowns show the points for each part of the answer, never the expected values.

**Which submission counts?** Your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, which ranks scored runs on
the public dataset. Your latest one that passed review (not your best one) goes into the final run: when the
hackathon ends, the organizers run it once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
That run weighs most when we pick the winners, ahead of your public score and the elegance of your system, so
build an agent that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario. See
[Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners).

**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
still open, so fix it and send it again.

**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
and scored runs always run in our sandbox.

**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 12 test and eval runs at a time, together, and can have up to
12 waiting; the next waits while other teams' runs start. The run page says how many runs are ahead of yours, and
`atira test-run --follow` prints it. See [the run queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue).

**How do I stop a run?** `atira cancel <run>`, or Cancel run on its run page. The sandbox is removed, the run fails
with "Cancelled by @you", and you can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run ends its
submission: the leaderboard ignores it, and you can submit again.

**Why do my requests get a 403 "Error 1010"?** The edge in front of our hosts refuses some default HTTP
clients, such as Python's `urllib`. Send your own `User-Agent` header (the starter kit does).

**Python says `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` on my Mac.** Python from python.org ships without CA certificates.
Run `Install Certificates.command` from its folder in Applications, or set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

**What can my agent reach during a scored run?** Our API (including the model proxy) and the challenge's
websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
run.

## Event details

- The event is on 10 October 2026.
- A team has up to five people.
- A scored run has 20 minutes on the clock; a test run has up to 2 hours.
- Ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).
=== building-an-agent
# Building your agent

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.

### Several browsers

To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:

```json
{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
```

Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
```

At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.

## Models

The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
up.

## What makes it hard, on purpose

The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
every page as adversarial and verify what you read.

## Tips

- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.

## Starter kit

[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.
=== run-contract
# How a run works

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge. It starts with a run token, gives your agent a task and
logins for the challenge's websites, and ends when your agent submits its answer or time runs out. Test runs and
scored runs both run your package in the [sandbox](#scored-run); you develop on your own machine with the scouting
logins.

## Develop locally, then test in the sandbox

RFQ has one public scenario, `public-1`: the websites as you see them.

1. **Develop locally** against the public websites with the scouting logins the organizers publish:
   `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` (in PowerShell: `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`) sets
   `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the websites and their logins, the JSON a run gets), each website's URL as
   `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL`, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the `brief`, `access`, `submission` and `answer_schema` of
   `GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` as JSON (`CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` is that address). There is no run token.
   Where the platform hosts models, they need no key: `--env` also exports each one's base URL and key, pointed at
   `atira models proxy` on your computer with `local` as the key, so run `atira login` once, then keep
   `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. Those calls are free, recorded and never ranked. Any other
   provider takes your own key.
   Nothing done with these logins counts.
   A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
2. **Test in the sandbox:** `atira test-run ./my-agent` uploads your package, starts a test run on `public-1` and
   opens its run page live. It runs in the same sandbox as a scored run, but for up to 2 hours instead of 20 minutes (keep it under
   20 to be safe), and the run page shows its
   score with the full breakdown. `atira cancel` stops it early.

## Inside a run

1. **Read the task:** `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with the header `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`
   returns:
   - `brief`: the task statement in markdown, with the rules;
   - `access`: one entry per website: `siteId`, `url`, and `credentials` (`username`, `password`);
   - `submission`: where the answer goes: `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` (POST it to that URL) or
     `{"kind": "site", "siteId": ..., "url": ...}` (submit it on that website, e.g. RFQ's configurator);
   - `answer_url` (API submissions only) and `answer_schema` (JSON Schema of the answer);
   - `started_at`, `expires_at`, and what the run has spent on LLM calls so far.
   - `llm_proxy_url`: the model proxy base with this run's token, `llm_providers` and `llm_base_urls` (each
     provider's proxy base), and `llm_env` (the SDK base-URL variables the run step gets).
   Keep the token secret: it is your agent's identity for this run.
2. **Work:** your agent logs into the websites with those credentials and collects what it needs. Its LLM calls
   go through our metering proxy: a hosted model's with the run token its key variable already holds, any other
   provider's with your own key (below).
3. **Answer** through the run's `submission` target. For an `api` target, `POST` the answer as JSON to
   `answer_url` with the same `x-api-key` header. For a `site` target, submit it on that website: the site
   forwards it to the platform, shows the same validation issues in German, and confirms with a receipt.
   - `400` with `issues`: the answer is malformed. Nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running, fix it and send
     it again.
   - `202`: accepted and final. The run ends, the token and the website logins stop working, and a test run
     returns its score and breakdown. Your agent then has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.

Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live. Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header
(`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.

## LLM calls

Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.

The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:

```
$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
```

`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:

| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |

The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.

### Your key

Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.

With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
as `x-api-key`:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
```

A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:

```python
import os
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
```

```javascript
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"

const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
```

A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.

**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
`401`.

A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
context.

### How cost is measured

Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
A model too new for the platform's price list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it, its long-context price
included. An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.

The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.

### Team secrets

Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:

```sh
curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
cannot be platform variabl

- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the

**Python says `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` on my Mac.** Python from python.org ships without CA certificates.
Run `Install Certificates.command` from its folder in Applications, or set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

**What can my agent reach during a scored run?** Our API (including the model proxy) and the challenge's
websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
run.

## Event details

- The event is on 10 October 2026.
- A team has up to five people.
- A scored run has 20 minutes on the clock; a test run has up to 2 hours.
- Ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).
=== building-an-agent
# Building your agent

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase) | `http://127.0.0.1:3128`, the only way out of the sandbox |
| `NO_PROXY` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` (CDP stays local) |

The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
ends without an answer scores 0.

## Browsers

export CHALLENGE_SCOUTING='{"challenge_id":"rfq","challenge_version":"6","scenario_id":"public-1","expires_at":253402300799000,"until_revoked":true,"access":[{"siteId":"tender-portal","url":"https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run","credentials":{"username":"u_9c3cb06a5d21b197","password":"REDACTED"}},{"siteId":"customer-portal","url":"https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run","credentials":{"username":"u_9c3cb06a5d21b197","password":"REDACTED"}},{"siteId":"erp","url":"https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run","credentials":{"username":"u_9c3cb06a5d21b197","password":"REDACTED"}},{"siteId":"mail","url":"https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run","credentials":{"username":"u_9c3cb06a5d21b197","password":"REDACTED"}}],"submission":{"kind":"site","siteId":"tender-portal","url":"https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run"},"brief":"# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer'''s supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material'''s price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder'''s mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer'''s quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position'''s stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification'''s pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.

import sys, time, pathlib, re
from urllib.parse import urljoin
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent))
from p2 import login, access  # noqa

site, out = sys.argv[2], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[3])
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
c, r = login(site)
for i, path in enumerate(sys.argv[4:]):
    t = time.monotonic()
    r = c.get(urljoin(access[site]["url"], path))
    name = f"{i:02d}_" + re.sub(r"[^\w.-]+", "_", path)[:80] + ".html"
    (out / name).write_text(r.text)
    print(f"{r.status_code} {time.monotonic() - t:.2f}s {len(r.text):>7} {r.url} -> {name} ct={r.headers.get('content-type')}")

"""ERP over HTTP: log in, pass the receipt gate by form post, then save given paths."""
import sys, time, pathlib, re
from urllib.parse import urljoin
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent))
from p2 import login, access  # noqa

site, out = sys.argv[2], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[3])
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
c, r = login(site)
base = access[site]["url"]
for attempt in range(4):
    r = c.get(urljoin(base, "/notice"))
    m = re.search(r'aria-label="Empfangsnummer: ([^"]+)"', r.text)
    if m:
        break
    print("notice status", r.status_code)
    time.sleep(1)
csrf = re.search(r'name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', r.text).group(1)
r = c.post(urljoin(base, "/notice"), data={"csrf": csrf, "receipt": m.group(1), "acknowledged": "yes"})
print("gate post", r.status_code, r.url)
for i, path in enumerate(sys.argv[4:]):
    t = time.monotonic()
    r = c.get(urljoin(base, path))
    name = f"{i:02d}_" + re.sub(r"[^\w.-]+", "_", path)[:80] + ".html"
    (out / name).write_text(r.text)
    print(f"{r.status_code} {time.monotonic() - t:.2f}s {len(r.text):>7} {r.url} -> {name}")
